remove: Unstructured steady-pace Assault Bike work immediately post-squats to mitigate negative interference on lower-body strength adaptations and patellofemoral fatigue.
improve: Structure Assault Bike intervals with a standardized work-to-rest ratio (e.g., 10-15 rounds of 20s maximal sprint : 40s active recovery) instead of non-specific pacing.
Enforce a 3-second eccentric cadence and a 2-3 minute inter-set rest period on Barbell Back Squats to ensure high mechanical tension across all 4 sets.
Control the pull-up descent with a full dead-hang reset at the bottom to maximize lat excursion and avoid kipping or momentum.
add: Horizontal press (e.g., Dumbbell Bench Press, 3 sets x 8-10 reps) to counter the vertical pulling volume and balance shoulder kinematics.
Posterior chain exercise (e.g., Romanian Deadlifts or Seated Leg Curls, 3 sets x 10-12 reps) to balance the quad-dominant squat loading.
Dynamic hip and ankle mobility prep (e.g., 90/90 hip switches and knee-to-wall ankle mobilizations) prior to back squats.
analysis.summary: This session delivers a potent foundational stimulus via multi-joint compound movements paired with cardiovascular conditioning. However, the routine lacks anterior-to-posterior upper-body balance and direct hamstring loading, leaving structural development incomplete. Refining the Assault Bike conditioning into precise interval blocks will improve anaerobic power output without prematurely blunting lower-body hypertrophy.

remove: Avoid performing duplicate isolation exercises targeting the exact same movement angle.
improve: Separate intense cardio and heavy strength by at least 6 hours, or place cardio at the end of the session.
Implement progressive overload by adding 1-2.5kg or 1 extra rep next session.
Maintain steady cadence (160-180 spm for running, 85-95 rpm for cycling) during Treadmill Interval Run.
add: Rotator cuff / scapular stability warm-up and 5 minutes of core bracing work.
Antagonist muscle pair work (e.g. Facepulls / Rear Delt flyes) for joint balance.
5-minute cool-down walk followed by hip flexor and hamstring dynamic stretching.
analysis.summary: Great hybrid session combining strength resistance (2 movements) with cardio endurance (3.5 km).
